_comment: Story dialogue: lines, then choices. Effects: cash, reputation, crew_influence, relationship {npc: n}, influence {district: n}, flags [..], turf_ally (crew), turf_give {corner: crew | 'player'}. Fictional and game-like.

boeta_sitdown.speaker: Boeta
lines: Word is the Tortel Laaities want a sit-down. Marlon Carelse himself.
He says the block's too small for two crews. He's not wrong.
Do we talk, or do we show them whose block it is?

choices.text: Set up the sit-down. Talking's cheaper than fighting.
choices.reply: Boeta: "Okay. I'll tell Marlon. Don't make me regret it."

choices.text: No talks. We send them a message on their own corner.
choices.reply: Boeta: "Then we do it at night, with the whole crew."

marlon_terms.speaker: Marlon Carelse
lines: Here's how it goes: the cafe corner is ours. The sand court, you can have.
Shake on it and nobody bleeds this winter.

choices.text: Shake on it. The cafe's yours, the court's ours.
choices.reply: Marlon: "Good. Keep your people off our side."

choices.text: Walk away. Nobody gives us anything; we take it.

spider_offer.speaker: Spider
lines: You held your own in Westridge. People talk out here too.
The Dune Cruisers could use friends on the other side of the gate.
Stand with us, and our boys won't move on your corners. What do you say?

choices.text: We stand with the Dune Cruisers.
choices.reply: Spider: "Then we're family, east of the gate."
Spider: "None taken. Just don't come crying."

faried_cut.speaker: Uncle Faried
lines: The stallholders saw you at the market. They feel safer.
The Stylers used to take a cut every month-end. Now people ask: will you?

choices.text: No cut. Keep your money, uncle. Just keep your eyes open for us.
choices.reply: Uncle Faried: "Then the whole market knows your name, and they'll say it kindly."

choices.text: A cut every month-end. Protection isn't free.
choices.reply: Uncle Faried: "...Fine. Here. Same as the last ones, then."

marlon_favour.speaker: Marlon Carelse
lines: We shook on the cafe. I keep my word, so now I ask for one.
The Vipers have been sniffing round the park. I want them to hear that the Laaities and you are one table.
Put your name next to mine for a week. That's all.

choices.text: Done. The Laaities and us, one table.
choices.reply: Marlon: "Good. Anyone who touches your corners answers to me."

choices.text: I'll keep my own name out of it.

spider_peace.speaker: Spider
lines: You said you'd stand alone. Then my boys found out what alone means.
I'm not a man who holds a grudge for sport. Take my hand, and the corners stay quiet.
Or don't. Either way I'll know where you stand.

choices.text: Fair. We stand with the Dune Cruisers after all.
